notes: Shopify store, direct HTTP fetch worked (no WAF), consistent with prior Home-Decor pass notes in notes/261.md. Checked full /collections.json (60 collections) for target terms: found exactly one match, 'Best Sellers' (handle best-sellers). No sub-structure exists (no 'Furniture Bestsellers' / 'Lighting Bestsellers' style children anywhere in the collections list) so emitted as a single undifferentiated row. Homepage header nav links directly to /collections/best-sellers, confirming it is a real navigation-level merchandising page, not a hidden/unlinked collection. Opened the page: it is a genuine PLP (product grid, no editorial/marketing copy). Per known site-specific defect from the prior pass (collections.json products_count is inflated 1.4x-5.75x on this store), did NOT trust the products_count=29 field. Instead enumerated the collection exhaustively via /collections/best-sellers/products.json?limit=250 (23 products, page 2 returned {"products":[]} confirming single-page completeness) and cross-checked against the rendered HTML product grid (23 unique /collections/best-sellers/products/<slug> hrefs, no pagination links present) - both methods agree exactly at 23. No other Bestsellers-type terms (Top Sellers, Popular, Customer Favorites, Trending) found in nav, footer, or the full collections.json list.

rows.evidence: Exhaustive /collections/best-sellers/products.json?limit=250 enumeration: 23 unique product ids, page 2 empty. Cross-checked: rendered HTML at /collections/best-sellers contains exactly 23 unique product slugs, no page=2 link present. Site's own collections.json products_count field reports 29 for this handle, but is known-inflated on this store (per prior extraction pass notes), so the exhaustive enumeration count was used instead.
